citation: Glessner House Museum, 'A servants' Christmas at Glessner House', The Story of a House (blog), 23 December 2012.
author: Glessner House Museum
locator: The whole post: the extra month's pay at Christmas 1894 for staff employed from 1 November 1893, from Frances Glessner's servants' journal, and the nine people it lists with their places and pay (Frederick Reynolds, butler; John Flear, footman; Mattie Williamson, cook; Alice Hassett; Antonie Gerstling, ladies' maid; Charles Nelson, coachman; Julia Johnson, housemaid; Annie Johnston, laundress; Martin), and the 1880 census of Charles Nelson living over the coach house with his wife Martha and son Norman.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-08 (T-3525) through a fetch that returned a summary of the post's text with short quoted segments. No archived snapshot verified.
note: The museum's reading of Frances Glessner's servants' journal for one Christmas. It gives Charles Nelson as the Glessners' coachman in 1894 and, by the 1880 census, already living over a Glessner coach house (the family's earlier home at Washington and Morgan Streets) with his wife and son.
what_it_supplies: Charles Nelson, coachman, in the Glessners' service by 1880 and in 1894
the staff of Christmas 1894, their places and some wages
what_it_does_not_supply: whether any of them were in the house in 1904, Mattie Williamson and Charles Nelson apart
